published_prior_art.cite: LeeGu2026DTBLCM proves the binary recursive determinant argument; its categorical discussion identifies the need for nonzero higher-state alternating polynomials rather than giving the all-q context-product.
LeeGu2026DTBLCM Appendix G gives a q=3 obstruction to binary nondegeneracy implying rank, not the proposed exact local-minor iff frontier.
AllmanMatiasRhodes2009 establishes generic-identifiability methodology, but not a nonzero polynomial certificate for every fixed categorical double-triangular graph.
ChenEtAl2025TensorRanks identifies mixed-type models through completeness and two-sufficient-measurement assumptions; the proposed equal-alphabet certified class relation is not supplied there.
LeeGu2026DTBLCM Theorem 1 identifies K for binary latent variables under double triangularity; the q-state consequence depends on the new determinant theorem.

AllmanMatiasRhodes2009 supplies three-view latent-class identification up to component labels; KivvaRajendranRavikumarAragam2021 aligns coordinates given a mixture oracle, not from the proposed certified q-state three-view construction.
LeeGu2026DTBLCM Theorem 2 is the binary double-triangular comparator; no inspected source subsumes the stated q>=3 certified-class result.
LeeGu2026DTBLCM Appendix G gives categorical failure examples, not the displayed positive q=3,K=3,J=8 certified no-pure-child witness.
LeeGu2026DTBLCM Theorems 1--2 give these binary full-rank, dimension, and identification conclusions.
Gu2026QUnfolding gives a constructive population Q-matrix recovery procedure with two pure items per attribute; KivvaRajendranRavikumarAragam2021 assumes a mixture oracle.
GuLiuXuYing2018QTest tests fit for a provisional Q-matrix, not simultaneous adaptive categorical local-minor and singular-value queries.

source_verification_receipts.version: public TMLR submission corresponding to arXiv:2505.18410; author publication page lists the TMLR 2026 article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves binary-latent double-triangular identification and explains that categorical latents require nonzero higher-state alternating-polynomial conditions; Appendix G gives the q=3 obstruction.

The published paper treats mixed-type observed variables, derives full-rank discretizations under completeness, and introduces a two-sufficient-measurement condition for latent-structure identification.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annals of Statistics 37(6A), 2009 author-hosted article PDF
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 2--3, abstract and introduction; pp. 10--11, three-way clumping/Kruskal discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses Kruskal's three-way latent-class argument, yielding generic identification up to latent-class label swapping rather than a latent-coordinate product recovery theorem.
The paper reconstructs graph and latent law from P(X) together with a mixture oracle; its coordinate correspondence construction explicitly uses oracle information.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 131 abstract; pp. 132--133 introduction; pp. 142--143 discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper constructively recovers a Q-matrix and K from the population tensor under at least two pure items per attribute, including polytomous responses; finite-sample singular-value replacement is expressly left for future work.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Turn the local-query handle into a theorem target with a finite input encoding, an explicit query bound in q,K,J, and a proof that each branch preserves all compatible realizations.
Add a compact q=3 coordinate-alignment worked table that explicitly computes the equality partitions, their refinements, and the resulting coordinate quotient for the displayed witness.
State a boundary corollary that precisely distinguishes the certificate condition from ordinary categorical nondegeneracy, including the smallest q=3 positive failure family.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 on the categorical determinant and coordinate-alignment kernel; retain the binary reduction strictly as a labeled regression/sanity proposition rather than a novelty claim.
